bug_description.original: A heap overrun occurs when substituting keywords in job files, specifically in the fio_keyword_replace function in options.c. The vulnerability is triggered when parsing options such as 'description=$ncpus', leading to a heap-buffer-overflow as detected by AddressSanitizer. The issue arises because the 'opt' pointer references a later position, causing incorrect memory access during keyword substitution. Functions involved include fio_keyword_replace, dup_and_sub_options, and fio_options_parse in options.c, as well as __parse_jobs_ini and parse_jobs_ini in init.c.
bug_description.normalized: During job-file parsing, an option line containing a reserved keyword such as `$ncpus` followed by trailing bytes reaches `fio_keyword_replace()`. The function saves the original buffer pointer in `o_org`, advances `opt` past the matched keyword, and then copies `opt - o_org - 1` bytes from the shorter suffix instead of `strlen(opt)`, causing a heap-buffer-overflow read during keyword substitution.

source.description: First project parser statement that materializes the attacker-controlled option line later duplicated and keyword-substituted. After the first witness line has already admitted the in-memory job buffer into a section, this inner-loop split returns the second line `$ncpus\xff` from the exact witness.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is exactly 11 bytes `5b ff 0a 24 6e 63 70 75 73 ff ff` (sha256 `8e89d111c802c763afae8e23e729795e32ed1e4e6c90ca21ae4dfab2d6ecf34b`). In `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput()` (`t/fuzz/fuzz_parseini.c:34-38`), bytes 0..9 are copied into `fuzzedini`, byte 10 becomes `type = 0xff`, and the copied buffer is NUL-terminated as `5b ff 0a 24 6e 63 70 75 73 ff 00` (`[\xff\n$ncpus\xff\0`). In that in-memory buffer this `strsep` returns the second line `$ncpus\xff`.

root_cause.code: memcpy(new + olen + len, opt, opt - o_org - 1);
root_cause.description: `fio_keyword_replace()` saves the original buffer pointer in `o_org`, advances `opt` past the matched keyword, and then computes the suffix copy length from the pointer delta `opt - o_org - 1` instead of the remaining suffix length. On the exact witness, this requests 5 bytes from a suffix whose actual remaining length is only 1; the patch corrects the third argument to `strlen(opt)`.
root_cause.note: The present guard `if (strlen(opt))` only proves the advanced pointer sees a non-empty tail. Because the length expression still measures distance from the stale `o_org` base pointer, the later source read is not bounded by that tail.

sink.code: memcpy(new + olen + len, opt, opt - o_org - 1);
sink.description: AddressSanitizer crash site. The same `memcpy` uses the miscomputed 5-byte length to read from `opt`, which points at the 2-byte tail `\xff\0`, so the source read crosses the right edge of the 8-byte heap buffer returned by `fio_option_dup_subs()`.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 5` at `options.c:5121` and says the faulting address is 0 bytes to the right of the 8-byte region allocated at `options.c:5086`.

parser_admitted.description: The first witness line `[\xff` passes this section-header gate with `sscanf` return value 1, so the parser creates a job section and reaches the inner option loop that later reads the second line.

tainted_value_origin.description: The heap object later overread is allocated here. `fio_option_dup_subs()` only expands `${VARNAME}` syntax, so the exact option string `$ncpus\xff` reaches `out` unchanged and `strdup` allocates the 8-byte region `$ncpus\xff\0` that AddressSanitizer reports.

coarse_trace.summary: After the first witness line is accepted as a section header, the in-memory INI parser splits out the second line `$ncpus\xff` as the option string for the current job.
Option parsing duplicates that line into a fresh 8-byte heap buffer unchanged because `${...}` environment substitution does not apply to the plain reserved keyword token `$ncpus`.
Keyword replacement matches `$ncpus` at offset 0, saves the original buffer pointer in `o_org`, derives `olen = 0`, advances `opt` to the one-byte suffix, and takes the `if (strlen(opt))` branch.
The suffix copy uses `opt - o_org - 1` instead of the remaining suffix length, so `memcpy` performs the observed 5-byte out-of-bounds read from the 8-byte heap buffer.

fine_trace.note: Source. After the first line `[\xff` from the same NUL-terminated witness buffer has already passed the section-header gate, the inner loop splits on the newline and returns the second line `$ncpus\xff`. That exact 7-byte option string is the attacker-controlled value later duplicated into the heap buffer that `fio_keyword_replace()` overreads.

`fio_options_parse()->dup_and_sub_options()` forwards the parsed option line into `fio_option_dup_subs()`. This helper only substitutes `${...}` environment references, so the plain reserved keyword survives unchanged and `strdup(out)` allocates the 8-byte heap buffer `$ncpus\xff\0` that AddressSanitizer later identifies as the overread region.

`fio_keyword_replace()` scans the duplicated option against the reserved-keyword table and the `$ncpus` entry matches at the start of the 8-byte buffer. The replacement loop therefore executes for this option instead of leaving the string untouched.

Inside the matching iteration, `o_org` saves the pre-advance `opt` value, aliasing the start of the 8-byte heap buffer. Later length arithmetic reuses this saved base pointer after `opt` itself moves to the suffix.
Because step 3 found the keyword at buffer offset 0, this subtraction derives `olen = 0`. There is no preserved prefix before the matched `$ncpus` token in the exact witness option.

Advancing by `strlen("$ncpus") + olen == 6` moves `opt` from the start of the 8-byte buffer to the one-byte tail `\xff` immediately before its terminating NUL. The saved alias from step 4 still points at the start of that same buffer.

After step 6 the remaining suffix length is exactly 1, so this guard is true and the suffix-copy path executes. The check proves only that some tail exists; it does not require the later `memcpy` length to fit inside the bytes remaining after the advanced `opt` pointer.

fine_trace.code: memcpy(new + olen + len, opt, opt - o_org - 1);
fine_trace.note: Root cause. The third argument is derived from pointer distance back to the saved alias `o_org`, not from the remaining suffix length. With `o_org` still at the start of the 8-byte buffer from step 4, `opt` advanced to offset 6 by step 6, and `olen = 0`, `opt - o_org - 1` evaluates to 5 even though step 7 established that only the one-byte suffix `\xff` remains before NUL. The patch fixes this exact obligation by replacing the length with `strlen(opt)`.

fine_trace.code: memcpy(new + olen + len, opt, opt - o_org - 1);
fine_trace.note: Sink. The same `memcpy` now reads 5 bytes starting at the 2-byte tail region `\xff\0`, so the source read extends 3 bytes past the 8-byte heap allocation from step 2. The saved AddressSanitizer trace reports `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 5` at `options.c:5121` and says the faulting address is 0 bytes to the right of that 8-byte region.

allocation_context.note: AddressSanitizer reports the invalid read is 0 bytes to the right of an 8-byte heap region allocated by `strdup(out)` here.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run executed `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_29564 run --version vulnerable --expect crash`, which fed `poc` to `/out/fuzz_parseini` and reproduced `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 5` in `fio_keyword_replace` with stack `dup_and_sub_options -> fio_options_parse -> __parse_jobs_ini -> parse_jobs_ini`.

format.name: 11-byte `fuzz_parseini` witness with section line `[\xff` and option line `$ncpus\xff`
format.contract: The only verified trigger is the exact 11-byte file `poc` (sha256 `8e89d111c802c763afae8e23e729795e32ed1e4e6c90ca21ae4dfab2d6ecf34b`). In `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput()`, bytes 0..9 are copied into `fuzzedini`, byte 10 is used as `type = 0xff`, and the copied bytes are NUL-terminated as the in-memory job buffer `[\xff\n$ncpus\xff\0`. In `__parse_jobs_ini()`, the first line `[\xff` passes the section-header `sscanf` gate, and the second line is duplicated unchanged as the 7-byte option string `$ncpus\xff`. That exact option shape makes `fio_option_dup_subs()` allocate the 8-byte heap buffer `$ncpus\xff\0`, lets `fio_keyword_replace()` match `$ncpus` at offset 0, save the original buffer pointer in `o_org`, advance `opt` to the one-byte tail `\xff`, and then reach the saved out-of-bounds `memcpy(new + olen + len, opt, opt - o_org - 1)` read of size 5.
